justification: The shipment record confirms the consignment's actual and chargeable weight is exactly 50.0 kg (no minimum-weight floor applies since 50 kg already exceeds the 25 kg floor per §1). Under §2, the two rate bands are written as "under 50 kg" (₹9.50/kg) and "over 50 kg" (₹8.25/kg) — both strict inequalities relative to 50 kg. A consignment weighing exactly 50 kg therefore falls into neither stated band, and no per-kg rate is written in the contract for this exact weight. This is not a case where one reading is merely inconvenient; it is a literal gap in the text, which the rate card's own ambiguities list independently corroborates. Neither the shipment facts nor any other clause (service level, special handling, etc.) supplies a tiebreaker — service level is standard with no special handling, so nothing else in the contract bears on which band should apply. Because the correct per-kg rate cannot be determined from the contract as written, and picking either band would mean inventing a rate the contract doesn't actually state, this must go to a human for a ruling (or a negotiated fix with the carrier) rather than being resolved by inference.

memo_narrative.what_happened: Alpine billed consignment AE-3005 (chargeable weight exactly 50.0 kg) at a flat amount, but the rate contract's per-kg bands are written as strictly under 50 kg or strictly over 50 kg, so no stated rate actually covers 50 kg exactly.
memo_narrative.why: Per §2, the two weight bands both use strict inequalities relative to 50 kg, leaving a genuine gap at exactly 50 kg that the contract text does not resolve; neither service level nor special handling on this shipment offers any tiebreaker.
memo_narrative.recommended_action: Escalate to Alpine Express's account manager for a ruling on which per-kg rate (₹9.50 or ₹8.25) applies to consignments at exactly 50 kg, and request the contract be amended to close this gap for future invoices.
